nodes.name: Summer sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer days power a short growing season for tundra, willow and lake algae; winters are dark and cold.

nodes.name: Lakes and rivers
nodes.desc: Glacial lakes and rivers such as Lake Clark and the Kvichak watershed carry sockeye to spawning grounds and feed lake algae.

nodes.name: Snow and winter cold
nodes.desc: Deep winter snow and cold limit food for herbivores and cover carcasses, shaping when bears, wolves and ravens eat.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and spawned-out salmon, returning nutrients to soil and water.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Grass-like plants of wet meadows and salt marshes. Sedges are a spring staple for brown bears, and the park notes salt marshes are key bear feeding areas.

nodes.name: Grayleaf willow
nodes.desc: A shrub willow of tundra and river flats. Willow twigs and buds feed moose, hares and ptarmigan.

nodes.name: Bog bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of tundra and bogs. Its leaves and berries are eaten by caribou, ptarmigan and bears.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae in lakes that feed zooplankton. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Caribou
nodes.desc: Tundra herds that eat sedges, shrubs and lichens. The park herds have fallen from about 200,000 to 30,000 for reasons not fully known.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: Large browser of willow and other shrubs in river valleys and boreal forest. Prey of wolves and bears.

nodes.name: Tundra vole
nodes.desc: Small rodent of wet meadows that eats sedges and grasses. Prey for stoats, gulls, ravens and bears.

nodes.name: Arctic ground squirrel
nodes.desc: Burrowing hibernator of tundra slopes. Brown bears are known to dig out and catch it.

nodes.name: Willow ptarmigan
nodes.desc: Grouse of tundra and shrub thickets that eats willow buds and berries. Preyed on by wolves, bears and stoats.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: Browser of willow twigs in boreal thickets. Main prey of Canada lynx and also eaten by wolves.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals drifting in lakes that graze algae and are the main food of sockeye in fresh water.

nodes.name: Sockeye salmon
nodes.desc: Returns from the sea to spawn in park lakes and streams; the Kvichak is described as the most productive sockeye watershed. Adults die after spawning.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: Small weasel that hunts voles, shrews, hares and ptarmigan under snow and over tundra.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: Boreal cat that depends heavily on snowshoe hares.

nodes.name: Mew gull
nodes.desc: Coastal and lakeshore gull that eats voles and scavenges salmon remains.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Omnivorous scavenger that picks over carcasses, including bear-left salmon and winter-killed game, and takes small animals.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Gathers on the coast to feed on spawning salmon and salt-marsh sedges; also eats berries, carrion and small and large prey.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Hunts caribou, moose and hares. A Lake Clark pack is documented as the only salmon-dependent wolf pack in the world.
